observations.why: A gate requiring signed manifests before shipping appeals to security and process control (conservation) and quality-of-craft assurance (competence).

observations.why: Citing past failures as justification for a gate appeals to security and stability as the governing good.

observations.why: Restating the gate as a key decision carries the same conservation and competence appeal, now under Xena's authorship with Quinton as principal.

Naming an owner assigns accountability for the gate's enforcement, appealing to mastery and responsible craft.
